newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE SURGES ON JGB ADVANCE, HITS CONTRACT HIGH.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE SURGES ON JGB ADVANCE, HITS CONTRACT HIGH.

text.p: Euroyen futures surged in afternoon Thursday trade, pushing the key March three-month contract to a fresh high of 99.26 before it fell back slightly, partly on growing bearishness on the economy, traders said.
The rise was also attributed to strong advances by key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures, which closed at their day's high of 126.97, the strongest in nearly four months.

One Japanese city bank apparently bought a large volume of JGB futures, and dealers were forced into active short-covering once the benchmark September contract rose past 126.70, which few in the market had expected to reach on Thursday, an industrial bank trader said.
The key March euroyen futures contract settled at 99.24, up 0.03 from Wednesday, with turnover a moderate 49,789 contracts. It moved from 99.21 to 99.26 over the course of the day.
Active sales late Wednesday helped clear long positions, giving futures some leeway to rise. Short-covering also emerged from those who had sold on Wednesday, traders said.

Traders said this, combined with growing bearishness about the economy, helped buoy futures and even enabled them to shrug off comments in an International Monetary Fund (IMF) report saying it would be desirable for Japan to begin raising interest rates later in the year.

"No matter what indicators people mention, the forecasts seem to be poor. Also, the growing sense that there will be no interest rate rise within this fiscal year reinforces the sense that the economy is sluggish," one city bank trader said. He added that once key March breaks decisively above 99.26, there is little to no resistance all the way to 99.30.

A different city bank trader agreed that a test of 99.30 is likely soon. He said he personally felt there was room to rise as far as 99.40, but that this would still take quite some time and a few more active buying factors.

Interest rate swap (IRS) rates fell across the board, with both Japanese and foreign banks moving to receive them, particularly at the longer end, although demand for receiving medium-term rates was also good. The 10-year IRS rate was quoted at 2.55/2.59 percent against 2.60/2.64 percent Wednesday, while the six-year IRS rate was at 1.96/2.00 percent against 2.01/2.05 percent.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) refrained from conducting its usual 0020 money market operation, leaving the market in a neutral condition.

By late afternoon key overnight call money was being traded at 0.39 percent, down from 0.45 and 0.46 percent in the morning, as demand fell ahead of Friday, the last day of the current reserves reporting period. Traders said the weighted average was likely to be 0.45 percent, although 0.44 percent was also possible. The weighted average was 0.47 on Wednesday.
Around 50 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued unchanged at 0.58 percent.
